_about: Vehicle, motor, recovery, environment and sensor assumptions for the IGT mock flight (tools/flight_profile/generate.py). Every number carries its source in the matching _source key. 'Rylan' = stated by the team; 'repo' = read from GroundStation26/FlightComputer26; 'assumed' = engineering estimate from public data where the repos have no spec. Swap in measured values as they become available; nothing else needs to change.

vehicle.source_file_note: the team's OpenRocket design (OpenRocket 24.12, rocket SWEET_V6, designer Alex Post; revision by Tate Engstrom and Chris McLaren: 'modified from V5 based on final CG measurement and body lengths in Midland, TX; IREC 2026'), from Rylan 2026-11-23. Geometry, masses, CG and Barrowman CP below come from the station's .ork import (backend/src/apogee_planner/ork.rs, test ork_import_reads_the_sweet_v6_design); tools/flight_profile/ork_sims.py compares this model with the design's six stored OpenRocket simulations
vehicle.length_source: .ork: nose 0.5334 + avionics 0.3858 + payload 0.5588 + recovery 0.5779 + DITW 0.6969 + 2 transition lips 0.0025 each + oxidizer tank 0.8128 + lower body 0.6668 + boattail 0.1492 m (14.39 ft; replaces the 'about 15 ft' estimate)
vehicle.diameter_source: .ork: carbon-fibre tubes radius 0.078232 m (6.16 in OD; the aluminium oxidizer-tank section is 0.1524 m, 6.00 in); OpenRocket's reference diameter is the maximum
vehicle.dry_mass_source: .ork: the stage mass override, 40.84 kg with overridesubcomponentsmass (the whole rocket) and CG 2.667 m, the as-built values the revision note says were measured in Midland. It is the burnout mass of every .ork simulation flown in the current configuration (IREC_STANDARDREPORT: 49.84 kg at ignition, 40.84 kg at burnout). It INCLUDES the motor hardware: the 14.32 kg 'EntireMotor_nofuel' mass object (run tank, valves, injector, chamber, nozzle; 'the entire motor without fuel') is one of the components it replaces. It EXCLUDES the propellant, which comes from our side (the GS fill reading plus the fuel estimate, motor.propellant_mass_kg; the planner from the fill it plans in the measured 15.85 L tank). The .ork's own component build-up is 34.32 kg (the burnout mass of the older TESTFIRE_NOTFULLOXTANK run, flown before the override was set), so 6.52 kg of the measured mass is not itemised in the design. Whether the 40.84 kg was weighed with the fuel grain installed is not recorded: if it was, about 1.1 kg (the assumed fuel) is double counted
vehicle.mass_breakdown_source: .ork component build-up as the station imports it (each section's own mass overrides kept; the main parachute is 3.49 kg because OpenRocket counts 16 x 6.1 m of 1 in tubular nylon lines), totalling 34.32 kg, plus the difference to the 40.84 kg stage override. Replaces the assumed breakdown (33.2 kg with an 8.6 kg run tank, 6.0 kg chamber and 2.5 kg plumbing: 17.1 kg of motor hardware against the measured 14.32 kg)
vehicle.cg_source: .ork: stage CG override (overridesubcomponentscg), the final CG measurement; OpenRocket puts the CG at 2.821 m at ignition with its 9.0 kg propellant
vehicle.cp_source: ork.rs Barrowman: Von Karman nose 2.0/rad at 0.267 m, 3 fins 8.33/rad at 4.048 m, boattail -1.05/rad at 4.307 m, the two 2.5 mm tank lips cancel; OpenRocket's own CP in IREC_STANDARDREPORT is 3.20-3.25 m between Mach 0.2 and 0.6 (it adds body lift and compressibility)
vehicle.run_tank_volume_source: measured: from Rylan 2026-11-23, 967.45 in^3 (x 0.016387064 L/in^3 = 15.8537 L); replaces the assumed 12 L. The apogee planner default and the firmware sim plant take it from here
vehicle.nose_source: .ork: 21 in Von Karman (haack, shape parameter 0) fibreglass nose cone, aft radius 0.078232 m; mass override 0.840 kg including the aluminium tip, rod, bulkhead, coupler and antennas
vehicle.fins_source: .ork: trapezoidal fin set on the lower body tube, 3 carbon-fibre fins (rounded cross-section, no cant), root 9.875 in, tip 5.4375 in, height 6.875 in, leading-edge sweep 3.25 in, thickness 0.26 in, trailing edge 1 in forward of the tube's aft end (leading edge 3.961 m from the nose)
vehicle.boattail_source: .ork: 'Boattail' transition (carbon fibre, haack, clipped) from 0.078232 to 0.053975 m radius over 0.149 m: base drag acts on the 108 mm aft circle (0.48 of the body area), as in OpenRocket; its length/diameter-step ratio of 3.1 is past OpenRocket's limit of 3 for boattail pressure drag, so there is none
vehicle.rail_buttons_source: .ork: magnetic rail buttons as 0.25 kg mass objects, top in the DITW container, bottom at the aft end of the lower body tube (0.16 m above the base); OpenRocket models no rail-button drag (aero.cd_extra covers it here)
vehicle.surface_roughness_source: .ork: nose, avionics, recovery and DITW tubes 'smooth' (20 um, OpenRocket), payload tube and fins polished, oxidizer tank and lower body 'normal' (60 um); the nose's finish is used, as the import does
vehicle.stability_source: ork.rs Barrowman with the measured dry CG: CNa 9.28/rad, CP 3.213 m, (3.213 - 2.667)/0.1565 = 3.49 cal; OpenRocket: 3.5-3.7 cal coasting in IREC_STANDARDREPORT, 2.8 cal at ignition with the propellant aboard
vehicle.pitch_inertia_source: I = factor * m L^2 / 12 (uniform rod). OpenRocket's longitudinal inertia for this design: 64.4 kg m^2 at ignition (factor 0.81) and 56.8 kg m^2 at burnout (0.87), IREC_STANDARDREPORT
vehicle.roll_source: assumed: about 0.2 deg of fin cant/misalignment gives about 1 rev/s near Mach 0.8, typical of amateur flight logs; roll time constant = 30 m / airspeed (the .ork fins have no cant)
vehicle.fc_station_source: .ork: the 'Avionics Bay' mass object, 0.719 m from the nose (in the avionics tube under the nose cone), 4.387 - 0.719 = 3.67 m from the base

motor.model_source: model 'measured' flies thrust_curve_csv (the datasets do); 'hybrid' flies the physics motor of hybrid_motor.py (motors/hybrid_motor.json, calibrated to the 2026-11-16 fire) for hybrid.fill_kg of GS fill reading, the tank at hybrid.tank_c (null = environment.pad_temp_c) and hybrid.supercharge_psig, on hybrid.grain (null = the spec's flight_grain, the motor_design/star_grain.stl star); its thrust gains (p_pad - p) x exit area with altitude and its propellant mass comes from the burn. generate.py --motor hybrid selects it
motor.source: repo-measured: thrust curve from the 2026-11-16 static fire, thrust = g*(KG1000 + KG50 unloading - burned) (extract_thrust.py; the rocket hangs from the 50 kg fill cell and presses the 1000 kg cell only once lifted), 9.19 kN s (7.6-10.1; the KG1000 alone gave 7.1), burn 5.65 s, peak about 3.3 kN; see motors/testfire_20261116.json. Propellant 6.7 kg = 5.6 kg N2O (KG50 fill cell before valve open) + about 1.1 kg fuel (assumed O/F 5), so delivered Isp about 140 s. total_impulse_ns null = the measured curve as is; a number rescales the curve to that impulse, by k^e on the thrust axis and k^(1-e) on the time axis (e = impulse_scaling_thrust_exponent; 0.5 = a bigger tank and injector), keeping the measured shape, and, with scale_propellant_with_impulse, the propellant mass at the measured delivered Isp. Nozzle exit diameter not in the repos (assumed 70 mm; only affects base drag while thrusting). Residual vapour 4% assumed. A +-3% 14 Hz feed-coupled oscillation is assumed (the smoothed curve removes it).

aero.source: OpenRocket technical documentation ch. 3.4 component build-up (friction with roughness limit and compressibility, base drag 0.12+0.13M^2 removed over the nozzle exit while thrusting, fin LE/TE pressure drag); +10% friction and 0.02 for rail buttons, fill/vent ports, joints. Transonic wave-drag rise of 0.3 from M 0.8 to 1.05 approximates a 5:1 ogive (no measured data). Gives Cd about 0.45-0.55 subsonic for a 30:1 body.

launch.ignition_source: repo: docs/integrated-ground-test.md 4.2: VB pilot at Launch + 10 s; replayed liftoff about t_ms 10000
launch.rail_source: 30 ft launch rail (9.144 m), the launch rod of the .ork's IREC_STANDARDREPORT and Simulation 1; effective travel taken as the full length
launch.rail_friction_source: Coulomb coefficient of the rail buttons on the aluminium rail (acetal/nylon on anodised aluminium, kinetic 0.1-0.2; mid value). Applied only on the rail, to the load across it: the weight's cross-rail component plus the cross-flow normal force (apogee_planner flight.rs rail_normal_accel). OpenRocket models no rail friction.
launch.tilt_source: IREC/SA Cup launch angle about 5 deg (DTEG allows up to 10); azimuth = tools/igt_csv.py default

attitude.source: assumed: aerodynamic pitch damping ratio 0.05-0.1 for finned rockets; hanging airframe lightly damped

recovery.drogue_source: assumed: FC detect_descent needs vel <= -4.25 m/s for 4 samples after Apogee + 80 ms (fcconfig.h), so about 1-1.5 s after true apogee
recovery.rates_source: .ork: the reefed canopy (1.778 m, Cd 0.55) opens at apogee and the main (3.556 m, Cd 1.4, both stay out) at 457.2 m: 1.37 m^2 and 15.3 m^2 of CdA on 40.84 kg give 24.6 m/s at 1500 m AGL and 6.8 m/s at the pad (OpenRocket IREC_STANDARDREPORT: ground hit 6.83 m/s); drogue kept at the 25 m/s first assumed, main 6.8 m/s (was 6). Canopy CdA solved from these rates. Fill times, opening-shock overshoot (Ck 1.3-1.4) and swing from Knacke, Parachute Recovery Systems Design Manual (NWC TP 6575) typical values; ejection/snatch impulses assumed (CO2 separation, shock-cord snatch)

environment.site_source: repo: FC LAUNCH_SITE_*_DEFAULT (fcconfig.h, IREC 2026, Midland TX); override with --site to match the station's Launch site setting
environment.temp_source: USSA-76 standard day; set e.g. +15 for a June afternoon in west Texas
environment.wind_source: task: 3-5 m/s with gusts; 1/7 power-law profile from 10 m, capped at 1.4x (reached near 110 m: the power law only describes the surface layer); Gauss-Markov gusts
environment.pressure_drift_source: assumed: slow synoptic drift, enough to leave a sub-metre baro offset at landing

imu.part: Bosch BMI088 (accel 24 g @ 1600 Hz ODR, gyro 2000 dps @ 2000 Hz ODR; repo accelerometer.c/gyroscope.c)
imu.source: BMI088 datasheet (BST-BMI088-DS001): accel 175 ug/sqrt(Hz), zero-g offset +-20 mg typ, 16 bit (1365 LSB/g at 24 g); gyro 0.014 dps/sqrt(Hz), zero-rate offset +-1 dps, 16.384 LSB/dps at 2000 dps. Range clipped just inside the FC's MAX_ACC = 24 g validator. Burn vibration and buffet assumed (no flight data in the repos); point-sampled like the FC, which takes the latest sample each cycle.

baro.part: Bosch BMP390 (OSR x8 pressure, ODR 100 Hz, IIR coef 3; repo barometer.c)
baro.alt_formula: 44330 * (1 - (p/p0)^0.1903), the FC's own (barometer.h ALT_PRES_CONST, BARO_HYPSOMETRIC_EXPONENT), p0 = pad pressure
baro.source: BMP390 datasheet (BST-BMP390-DS002): relative accuracy +-3 Pa, absolute +-50 Pa, raw RMS noise a few Pa at x8 (we use 2 Pa before the IIR); IIR coef 3 as configured; static-port Cp and AV-bay lag assumed (port-location dependent); CO2 ejection pressure pulse in the AV bay assumed (well known in amateur rocketry, magnitude varies)

gps.rate_source: repo: FC replay delivers GPS at 10 Hz (ground_test.c IGT_GPS_PERIOD_MS)
gps.source: assumed u-blox class receiver: CEP about 2.5 m; loses lock under boost (>4 g dynamic-model limit) and reacquires a few seconds after burnout. Rows are omitted during the dropout (the FC replay bridges the gap; the ascent filter does not use GPS).

output.source: repo: docs/integrated-ground-test.md 4.2 recommends IMU 100 Hz, baro 50 Hz, GPS 10 Hz. The FC disables the IMU in descent (kalman.c descent_initialize), so IMU rows drop to imu_descent_hz from apogee + imu_full_rate_after_apogee_s, except +-window around the main deployment and the landing. The replay interpolates linearly between rows.
